display.description: Every AI call routed through ai-meter (:8107): who is calling, which provider and model, what it costs at the reference price table, how slow it is, whether the metering itself is healthy, and how admission control is doing against z.ai's rate limit. Success Rate and Failures count only the calls a provider had to answer; the calls ai-meter sends back with a 429 are in Not Admitted. Feeds the AI Upstream Failure Rate rule; built after the 2026-10-17 Z.ai 1113 outage (coding-plan key on the general endpoint) went unobserved for hours.
display.name: AI Meter — Routed AI Calls

display.description: Calls the proxy keeps in flight at z.ai right now. The allowance starts at the configured ceiling, drops by one per "too much at once" answer and grows back by one after 30 quiet seconds.
display.name: Limit (now)

display.description: Calls queued inside the proxy for provider room, in arrival order. Each one is a client waiting on ai-meter; a call that outlives the wait budget is sent back with a 429 (Not Admitted).
display.name: Waiting (now)

display.description: How calls to the gated provider ended in the last 24 hours: admitted (sent and answered), absorbed (a "too much at once" answer was retried and the call succeeded), timeout (no slot within the wait budget: the client got a 429 and sends the call again), circuit (a usage window is spent: 429 until its reset), gave_up, cancelled (the client went away).
display.name: Admission Outcomes (24h)

display.description: Per gated provider: calls sent (in flight), calls queued for room (waiting), and the allowance the proxy currently keeps (limit). The limit drops by one per "too much at once" answer and grows back after a quiet half minute.
display.name: Admission: In Flight, Waiting, Limit

display.description: Mean seconds a call to the gated provider waited in the proxy's queue before it was sent. The wait is part of the time to first byte the user sees.
display.name: Avg Admission Wait

display.description: Mean wall time of a completed call over the last 15 minutes, streaming and not.
display.name: Avg Duration

display.description: Completion tokens per second of generation over the last 15 minutes, all models: output tokens divided by wall time minus time to first byte.
display.name: Avg Output Speed

display.description: Mean time to the first streamed byte over the last 15 minutes (streaming calls only). This is the wait a user feels before text appears, and it includes the time the call queued in the proxy for provider room (see Avg Admission Wait), not only the provider's own first-token time.
display.name: Avg TTFT

display.description: Share of prompt tokens served from the provider's prompt cache (cached is a subset of prompt). Higher is cheaper: a cached input token costs a fraction of a fresh one. Only meaningful for models with prompt caching.
display.name: Cache Hit Rate

display.description: Requests through the proxy over the last 24 hours, every outcome. A call the client sends again after a retry answer counts again.
display.name: Calls (24h)

display.description: Mean wall time per completed call per model.
display.name: Avg Duration by Model

display.description: Calls per minute that failed for real: the provider's own 4xx or 5xx, a call the proxy gave up retrying, a client that went away (499). The proxy's own retry answers are not in here (see Not Admitted). Orange past 2/min, red past 10/min.
display.name: Failures / min

spec.name: A
spec.query: ((sum(rate(ai_meter_requests_total{code=~"4..|5.."}[5m])) - (sum(rate(ai_meter_admission_outcomes_total{outcome=~"timeout|circuit"}[5m])) or vector(0))) or vector(0)) * 60 or vector(0)

display.description: Share of a provider's calls that failed, not counting the calls ai-meter sent back. This is the panel that names which provider is failing while the overall success rate drops.
display.name: Error Rate by Provider

spec.name: A
spec.query: 100 * ((sum by (upstream) (rate(ai_meter_requests_total{code=~"4..|5.."}[5m])) - (sum by (upstream) (rate(ai_meter_admission_outcomes_total{outcome=~"timeout|circuit"}[5m])) or (sum by (upstream) (rate(ai_meter_requests_total[5m])) * 0))) or (sum by (upstream) (rate(ai_meter_requests_total[5m])) * 0)) / (sum by (upstream) (rate(ai_meter_requests_total[5m])) - (sum by (upstream) (rate(ai_meter_admission_outcomes_total{outcome=~"timeout|circuit"}[5m])) or (sum by (upstream) (rate(ai_meter_requests_total[5m])) * 0)))

display.description: Failed calls per minute by HTTP status, without the proxy's own 429 answers (those are in Not Admitted). 499 is a client that went away before the answer.
display.name: Failures by Code

spec.name: A
spec.query: sum by (code) (rate(ai_meter_requests_total{code=~"4..|5..", code!="429"}[5m])) * 60 or label_replace(clamp_min((sum(rate(ai_meter_requests_total{code="429"}[5m])) - (sum(rate(ai_meter_admission_outcomes_total{outcome=~"timeout|circuit"}[5m])) or vector(0))) * 60, 0), "code", "429", "", "") or label_replace(vector(0), "code", "429", "", "")

display.description: Seconds since SigNoz last scraped the proxy's metrics endpoint. Past 2 minutes every panel on this dashboard is stale, whatever it shows.
display.name: Metrics Freshness

display.description: Calls inside the proxy right now, all providers. In flight means the client is waiting on ai-meter; it says nothing about whether the provider is throttling (see Admission).
display.name: In Flight

display.description: Concurrent calls per client (the service holding the key) over time. One client hogging the provider is visible here first.
display.name: In Flight by Client

display.description: Concurrent calls per model over time.
display.name: In Flight by Model

display.description: Concurrent calls per provider over time. A line that sits pinned at z.ai's cliff (about 6 to 9 before admission control) is the shape that produced the 429 storms.
display.name: In Flight by Provider

display.description: Every combination with a call in flight right now, busiest first. An empty table means nothing is waiting. `none` is a call whose request body named no model (embeddings, non-chat routes).
display.name: In Flight: Provider x Model x Client

display.description: Share of the last 24 hours' calls whose tokens could not be read from a 2xx answer or written to the ledger. The call itself succeeded; only its tokens and cost are missing. A few single calls are normal (7 of 13,700 on 2026-11-26); a jump means a provider changed its usage format.
display.name: Not Metered (24h)

display.description: Calls per minute whose tokens could not be read or written. A spike under one provider is a changed usage format; one under one client is a request shape the meter does not parse.
display.name: Metering Errors / min

display.description: Calls, tokens and outcome per model over the last 24 hours, one row per model. calls = not admitted + failed + served: not admitted were answered 429 by ai-meter (the client sends them again), failed got the provider's own error or the client went away, success is served over served plus failed. Spend is not a column on purpose: tables cannot run the priced queries, and a 24-hour increase of the cost counter would report a restatement as spend (see the spend panels above).
display.name: Models: Last 24 Hours

display.description: Calls per minute that ai-meter answered 429 itself: the call waited out its budget (30 s) without a slot at the gated provider, or a usage window is spent. Each costs its client the wait and a re-sent request; a client that honors Retry-After sends the call again and it keeps its place. Orange or red for long means more sessions are running than the gate's allowance serves (see Admission).
display.name: Not Admitted / min

display.description: Retry answers the proxy gave clients per minute, by outcome: timeout (no slot within the wait budget, retry at once) and circuit (a usage window is spent, retry at its reset).
display.name: 429 Answers From ai-meter / min

display.description: Share of the gated provider's requests in the last 5 minutes that ai-meter answered 429 itself: the gate's contention in one number, demand against the allowance. Orange from 15 %, red from 30 %: start fewer parallel sessions, wait, or change the gate's limits (docs/services/ai-meter.md).
display.name: Not Admitted: Share (5m)

display.description: The three outcomes of a request, what the colors mean, where the traces are.
display.name: How to read this dashboard

spec.text:
**How to read this page.** Every request through ai-meter ends one of three ways. **Served**: the provider answered 2xx. **Not admitted**: ai-meter itself answered 429, because the call waited out its 30 s budget without a slot at the gated provider, or a usage window was spent; the answer says when to send the call again and the call keeps its place, so it is a delay, not a failure. **Failed**: everything else, including the provider's own 4xx and 5xx and clients that went away. Success Rate, Failures and the table below count not-admitted calls as neither success nor failure.

**Red means act now.** Failures, missing metering, a spent usage window or a stale proxy are red the moment they happen. Not Admitted turns orange and red by its size: more sessions are running than the gate's allowance serves. Start fewer, wait, or change the gate's limits (docs/services/ai-meter.md).

**Every call is also a trace.** SigNoz's own AI views show the same calls by model, tokens, time to first token and errors: [AI observability overview](/ai-observability/overview) and [AI explorer](/ai-observability/explorer). Spans carry metadata only, never a prompt.

**The page loads once.** To keep it live, pick an interval in the top-right menu.

display.description: Mean prompt tokens per routed call over the last 15 minutes, cached or not: the size of the context each call carries. It drives both cost and time to first byte.
display.name: Prompt / Call

display.description: True while z.ai reports a spent usage window: the proxy sends nothing until the reset time the answer named and answers every call 429.
display.name: Quota Exhausted

display.description: HTTP 429 answers from z.ai meaning a usage window is spent. The calls that met one were answered 429 until the reset; Quota Exhausted above is red while it lasts.
display.name: Quota Answers (24h)

display.description: HTTP 429 answers from z.ai meaning "too much at once". Each one lowers the allowance by one and is retried by the proxy, so a call behind one is not lost by itself.
display.name: Rate-Limit Answers (24h)

display.description: Rate-limit and quota answers z.ai gave the proxy, per minute, by business code: 1302 is "too much at once", 1308 a spent usage window.
display.name: 429 Answers From z.ai / min

display.description: Requests per minute per client (the service holding the key), every outcome.
display.name: Requests by Client

display.description: Requests per minute per model, split by HTTP status. A 429 line under a model is mostly ai-meter sending calls back (Not Admitted); a 5xx or 499 line is a real failure.
display.name: Requests by Model x Code

display.description: Requests per minute per provider, every outcome.
display.name: Requests by Provider

display.description: Completed requests per minute over the last 5 minutes, all providers and every outcome: served, not admitted (sent back by ai-meter with a 429) or failed.
display.name: Requests / min

display.description: How often the proxy process started in the last 24 hours. Every deploy restarts it and every start resets the counters; a count that climbs without a deploy is a crash loop.
display.name: Starts (24h)

display.description: Calls whose trace span never reached SigNoz (the OTLP endpoint rejected it or the export queue dropped it). Those calls are metered but invisible in the AI observability views.
display.name: Span Export Failures (24h)

display.description: Spans per minute by how handing them to SigNoz went: ok, failed, dropped.
display.name: Span Export by Outcome

display.description: Completion tokens per second of generation: output tokens divided by (wall time minus time to first byte). Generation speed of the model behind the provider, independent of queueing.
display.name: Output Speed by Model

display.description: Reference cost of the last 24 hours: the tokens of every priced model at today's price table. It is not read off the cost counter, whose steps are price restatements, not spend.
display.name: Spend (24h)

display.description: Reference cost per hour: tokens x the price table in services.ai-meter.costs, computed at query time so a late price row restates the whole history. What the traffic WOULD cost pay-as-you-go, not what the coding plan bills.
display.name: Spend Rate

display.description: Reference cost per hour per client, summed over the priced models it calls.
display.name: Spend Rate by Client

display.description: Reference cost per hour per priced model.
display.name: Spend Rate by Model

display.description: Reference cost since the ledger began, at today's price table. The proxy replays the ledger at every start, so a price change reaches this number from the next start on; unpriced models count as 0.
display.name: Spend (all-time)

display.description: Share of the last 5 minutes' calls that the provider answered 2xx. Calls ai-meter sent back with its own 429 (see Not Admitted) count as neither success nor failure: the client sends them again and they keep their place. Red under 90 %, orange under 98 %. Empty while no call is in the window.
display.name: Success Rate (5m)

display.description: Tokens per minute per client, all kinds.
display.name: Tokens by Client

display.description: Tokens per minute. cached is a subset of prompt (the part served from the provider's prompt cache).
display.name: Tokens by Kind

display.description: All tokens per minute over the last 5 minutes: prompt, cached and completion.
display.name: Tokens / min

display.description: Share of the last hour's calls whose span reached SigNoz. One hour, like the AI Trace Export Silent rule, so a broken export shows within the hour.
display.name: Traced Calls (1h)

display.description: Mean time to first streamed byte per model, queue time in the proxy included.
display.name: Avg TTFT by Model

display.description: Calls rejected before any provider was contacted: unknown client key.
display.name: Unauthorized (24h)

display.description: True while SigNoz scrapes the proxy's metrics endpoint. False means the proxy is down or the scrape is broken, and every other panel is stale.
display.name: Reachable

display.description: Time since the proxy last started. Every cumulative counter restarts here, so a short uptime explains a small all-time spend.
display.name: Process Uptime
